title: Code quality
description: Changes a maintainer would approve: correct, tested at the behavior level, secure, simple.

criteria.title: Correct, including edges
criteria.ask: Did you try empty input, huge input, concurrency, failure of every dependency and a second run?
criteria.evidence: The edge cases exercised and what happened.

criteria.title: Tests prove behavior
criteria.ask: Would a test fail if the behavior regressed? Are tests testing the code or only its shape?
criteria.evidence: New or changed tests, and proof that they fail without the change.

criteria.title: Secure by construction
criteria.ask: Untrusted input, paths, commands, secrets, authorization: any new risk surface?
criteria.evidence: The inputs that cross a trust boundary and how each is validated.

criteria.title: Compatible
criteria.ask: Public APIs, file formats, CLI flags and exit codes: unchanged unless the change was authorized?
criteria.evidence: The public surface touched, or a statement that none was.

criteria.title: Readable
criteria.ask: Names, structure and comments that match the surrounding code?
criteria.evidence: A read-through of the diff as a reviewer; what you renamed or simplified.

criteria.title: Failures are explained
criteria.ask: When it fails, does the user or caller learn what happened and what to do?
criteria.evidence: The error messages produced by forcing the main failures.

criteria.title: No dead or speculative code
criteria.ask: Anything unused, duplicated, or built for a future that has not been asked for?
criteria.evidence: What was removed; searches proving the rest is used.

criteria.title: Docs and changelog follow
criteria.ask: Does every document that mentions this behavior now say the truth?
